headline: Red Sox collapse in Pittsburgh as pitching hits a new low
morning_brew: I watched that loss yesterday through my fingers like a horror movie and the ending somehow got even uglier. Sandoval had a total disaster on the mound, coughing up seven runs in four innings, and once that arson squad of a bullpen took over, the game was essentially cooked. We had a two-and-a-half-hour rain delay that sucked every ounce of life out of the park, but let's be real, this team looked checked out long before the skies opened up.

Losing Masataka Yoshida to a hamstring strain is just the rotten cherry on top of a miserable sundae. We are fighting for every single inch in the AL East, and losing a bat like his for ten days is a massive kick to the gut at the worst possible time. My neighbor Rick has been busy filing his daily umpire dossier, but he is starting to pivot to the theory that the baseball gods have a personal vendetta against us this season, and after watching us strand runners while the Pirates teed off on our arms, I am starting to think he is onto something.

It is the same exact movie, just a different, worse remake, and I am getting real tired of watching the same tragic ending. We need a massive reset tonight against Arizona at Fenway Park, because if we do not start stringing some wins together, this season is gonna slip through our fingers like cousin Jimmy trying to field a lazy pop fly. I will be at the Fens tonight, praying for a clean outing and some actual run support before I lose my mind.

news_digest.headline: Red Sox place Masataka Yoshida on IL with hamstring strain
news_digest.dans_take: Just our luck to lose our best contact bat right when we need to start climbing back into the fight.
